$comment: SIBLING REGISTRY — files and templates that must move together.
WHY THIS EXISTS — 2026-09-15. Of 173 behaviour commits in 60 hours, 27 were
PARTIAL and every one had the same shape: a fix landed on one code or prompt
path and not its sibling. The `fixing-sibling-paths` skill already described
the failure class in prose and did not prevent a single one of the 27 — prose
is advisory, and an agent that does not invoke the skill never reads it. This
file makes the sibling relationship DATA, so two mechanical consumers can use
it: scripts/admin/check-sibling-paths.js (pre-push gate) and
tests/unit/sibling-parity.test.ts (structural parity, runs in the normal suite).
ADDING A SET is one entry. Keep `reason` to one line and name the axis — the
gate prints both, so the person it blocks learns what to look at.
FIELDS
id        stable slug, used in the gate output
axis      the recurring split this set belongs to
reason    one line: why these move together
members   repo-relative paths; ALL must change together (see severity)
severity  'block' — the only accepted value. A 'warn' tier existed for one
day; the owner retired it on 2026-09-15: EVERY set blocks, and the
Siblings-Checked marker (same-commit or vouching) is the one escape.
The gate rejects any other value rather than reading it as block.
generators / critics
A set may declare these INSTEAD of `members` (axis
generator-vs-critic). The rule is different and looser on purpose:
a commit touching the set must touch at least ONE generator AND at
least ONE critic, not every member. Three judges of one generator
are not siblings of each other; each is a sibling of the generator.
The disease this treats: a rule is added to a judge and the
generator is never told, so the page is penalised for something it
was never asked to do.
parity    optional structural assertions for tests/unit/sibling-parity.test.ts:
metadataKeys: true  -> the ---METADATA--- JSON example in every
member declares the same top-level keys
anchors: ["..."]     -> every member contains each literal string
ruleAnchors: [{critic, generator, note}] -> for a generator-vs-critic
set, a rule named on the critic side must have
its counterpart instruction on the generator side
ESCAPE HATCH — put `Siblings-Checked: <reason>` in the commit message when the
siblings genuinely need no change. It is a statement, not a silencer: write why.
A push whose FULL range covers every member passes without a marker, so a fix
split across two commits in one push is fine.

sets.reason: scene-expansion.txt is the per-page gap-fill/fallback template for the same Art Director contract scene-expansion-all.txt drives on the live beats path; a rule or metadata field on one and not the other silently reads as absent on whichever path runs.

sets.axis: beats text writer vs trial writer
sets.reason: story-text-from-beats.txt (the live beats path, every full story) and story-trial.txt (the live /try funnel writer) both write page prose under the same shared rules; a prose rule that becomes a promptBuilders constant reaches a path only through the placeholder that path declares, so a new one is declared at both sites or it silently reads as absent there. This set now also carries the retired trial-vs-full-writer axis: the trial path has repeatedly lagged the full path by weeks. story-unified.txt / story-unified-imagefirst.txt were members until 2026-09-15, when both were deleted as unreachable (docs/decisions.md).

parity.anchorsNote: only {PAGE_OPENING_VARIETY} is genuinely declared by both live prose writers. {RISK_FRAMING} and {AD_COMPOSITION} were anchors of the deleted unified-writer sets and are NOT declared by story-text-from-beats.txt — the beats chain carries risk framing inside {TELLING_RULES} on the arc prompts and composition on the Art Director. Asserting them here would assert a parity into existence that does not hold.

sets.reason: story-text-audit.txt (arc-informed) and story-text-audit-blind.txt (the blind reader) feed ONE parser and ONE merge (parseFaultLines / mergeAuditFindings, textRefine.js), and that merge dedupes on the CATEGORY TAG: same page + same category + different auditor is folded into one finding. So the FAULT-line output contract and the category vocabulary are shared state — a category name that gains a meaning on one side and not the other either folds two distinct faults into one or splits one fault into two. The question SETS are deliberately different, which is what the Siblings-Checked marker is for; the contract they share is not.

story-text-proofread.txt (the lector) and story-text-diff.txt (the diff pass) feed the SAME parser and applier (parseLectorFindings / applyLectorFindings, textRefine.js:996-999), so a change to the quoting or span contract on one breaks the other's output against the shared applier.

image-evaluation.txt and image-inventory-unified.txt both describe the per-figure inventory the blind judge (image-prompt-compliance.txt) consumes; a schema change on one makes the two inventories incomparable.

sets.axis: Art Director VB authoring vs writer VB authoring
sets.reason: the Visual Bible is authored at two LIVE sites — the all-pages Art Director on the beats path (every full story) and the trial writer — and a rule about what a VB entry must state has to exist at both. The two pre-beats unified writers were members until 2026-09-15, when they were deleted as unreachable (docs/decisions.md).

parity.anchorsNote: the VB entry keys both live authoring sites genuinely declare today. `"size"` was anchored until 2026-09-15 and was dropped when the free-text size field was replaced by the `scaleClass` enum as the single source of scale truth; story-trial.txt still declares a PER-PAGE `size` on its scene-hint objects, which is a different field with a different consumer and is deliberately not anchored here. `"states"` is anchored since 2026-09-15 — owner ruling, every bible-authoring site declares it. `"vantages"` stays deliberately NOT anchored: it is absent from scene-expansion-all.txt, which is a real divergence, not a parity target to assert into existence.

sets.axis: production repair vs user regeneration vs entity char-fix
sets.reason: repairPipeline.js, routes/regeneration.js and entityConsistency.js each invoke character repair by their own assembly; a guard or gate added to one leaves the other two entry points unguarded.

sets.axis: cover path vs page path cast assembly
sets.reason: coverComposite.js and compositeCastBuilder.js both resolve a hint-string name to a character and both hand-roll parts of it; a resolver or costume-key fix on one leaves the other resolving by raw name.

sets.axis: trial idea route vs its Test Lab mirror
sets.reason: the /try idea route (server/routes/trial.js) and the Lab's idea stage (server/lib/testlab.js, marked `route mirror:`) hand-assemble the SAME character line, category context and landmark text; a copy kept by hand at both is how the raw storyTheme ID shipped into every life-skill prompt as "the child plays at being a farm" (2026-09-15). Shared text belongs in one constant both require.

sets.axis: Test Lab stage vs production call site
sets.reason: testlab.js re-implements the call that evalPipeline.js makes in production; when they drift the Lab measures something production never runs (version pinning, cast lists, model ids).

image-generation.txt is the only instruction the illustrator receives; image-evaluation.txt, image-semantic.txt and image-prompt-compliance.txt are the three judges that score the result. A rule added to a judge and not to the generator penalises a page for something it was never asked to do.

ruleAnchors.note: D-24 is CATASTROPHIC/CRITICAL for a mark painted on a figure, and the template forbade lettering only. The generator half is one exported constant (NO_CHARACTER_MARKING_RULE, promptBuilders.js) filled into this placeholder; that it reaches the BUILT prompt is pinned in tests/unit/generator-critic-rule-reach.test.ts, because a placeholder nobody fills is stripped silently.
D-16b is MAJOR when a hand holds something the scene never named while a named object is absent. The generator half is HANDS_HOLD_ONLY_NAMED_RULE, same mechanism and same reach test.

sets.reason: scene-review.txt critiques the briefs scene-expansion-all.txt authors; a check the reviewer applies that the Art Director was never given produces a finding no rewrite can satisfy.

story-text-proofread.txt and story-text-audit.txt judge prose written under story-text-from-beats.txt (the live writer on every full story) and story-trial.txt (the /try funnel); a style or structure rule the auditor enforces must be a rule the writer was given, or every story is corrected after the fact instead of written right. The generator was story-unified.txt until 2026-09-15, when that template was deleted as unreachable — it had not been the live prose writer since the beats pipeline shipped.

avatar-evaluation.txt gates avatars generated from avatar-main-prompt.txt; a criterion the judge rejects on must be an instruction the generator carries, or the retry loop burns paid calls chasing a rule nobody stated.

empty-scene-qc.txt is validateEmptyScene's judge of the plate empty-scene.txt paints; a check the judge applies that the plate author was never given is a blind grade, which is exactly how the reserved-corner and geometry findings arose. The shared half stays shared: GEOMETRY_DIMENSIONS (sceneGeometry.js) writes the author's geometry block and the judge's {GEOMETRY_CHECK} from one source. Extracted from evalPipeline.js string literals on 2026-09-15.

cover-evaluation-notes.txt is the cover-only preamble the evaluator is given (viewer gaze, flat title, and the text regime), and cover-composition.txt plus the cover hint assembly in coverIterate.js is what the cover was painted from; a text or gaze rule tightened on one side and not the other scores a cover for a brief it never had. Extracted from evalPipeline.js string literals on 2026-09-15 so this pair can name a path instead of a 5,000-line module.
plan-check.txt checks the page plan story-beats.txt produces; a constraint the checker counts must be a constraint the planner was told to satisfy.

server/lib/jobHeartbeat.js writes story_jobs.updated_at and server/routes/jobs.js is the only reader that kills a job for a stale one (two detectors, poll-time and stale-sweep); a change to when or whether the worker heartbeats, or to the timeout that reads it, is meaningless unless both sides move together.

scene-iteration.txt (the default rewrite) and scene-iteration-free.txt (the looser rewrite chosen when the composition is failing) are filled by ONE call site with one placeholder map; a rule or placeholder added to one is silently absent on whichever template that page's iterate selected.

sets.axis: first Art Director vs rewrite Art Director
sets.reason: A page brief is authored at FOUR sites: the two Art Director templates that write it the first time, and the two iterate templates that REWRITE it when the render proves it unbuildable. The rewrite replaces the brief wholesale and becomes the page's contract with the image model, so a rule only the first author holds is a rule one repair round deletes. Measured 2026-09-17 over the 11 stored iterate rounds of staging job_1789584708605_rts4wqupm and job_1789506283204_3kxqshifx: 11 of 11 rewrites dropped `shot`, `landmarkView` and every character's `depth` and `looksAt`, and emitted no `wornItems` row at all, where the brief each replaced carried all of them. This set is why that cannot happen silently again: touch an Art Director template and the gate asks what the rewriter gets.

parity.anchorsNote: Placeholders, not prose: each is ONE exported constant filled at all four sites, so the anchor proves the rule reaches the template and tests/unit/ad-iterate-parity.test.ts proves the constant reaches the BUILT prompt byte-identically. Three iterate-only placeholders stay deliberately unanchored because they have no Art Director counterpart to keep in step: {OBJECT_ID_STABILITY} (the Art Director MINTS the ids, so it has none to substitute), {DECLARED_TRAIT_VERBATIM} (declared where the drift was measured — see DECLARED_TRAIT_VERBATIM_RULE), and {MAX_CHARACTERS_PER_SCENE} (the image model’s face cap, which the Art Director expresses as its own staging rules).

withinFile.axis: streaming vs non-streaming provider entry points
withinFile.reason: every provider entry point in textModels.js must guard its prompt string; callOpenRouterAPI shipped without it while all seven siblings had it.
withinFile.excludeReason: callClaudeAPI is a dispatcher over the provider entry points, not one itself — it guards nothing because the callee does.

withinFile.reason: collectStagedFigures (names a Visual Bible figure onto the rewriter's locked cast) and partitionAnchoredObjects (lets a rewrite ADD a Visual Bible id) are the two sites that put a bible entity on a page; fa2cb3696 gated one on the bible's structured page range and not the other, so the creature the allow-list refused on p13/p16 was still staged there by its plan-line name. Both must consult vbEntityCoversPage.
withinFile.excludeReason: module.exports is the terminator that closes partitionAnchoredObjects' block so its body is measured exactly; it is not a staging site.
